title: Developing Team Members With a Proactive Attitude
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that proactivity, anticipating problems and opportunities and acting before being asked, is a learnable behavior shaped primarily by leader response, not innate personality. It identifies two conditions that produce proactive team members: a clear expectation that initiative is wanted, and recognition for taking initiative even when the resulting outcome falls short. The piece recommends practicing proactivity as a group exercise, brainstorming upcoming events and possible pre-emptive actions together, before shifting to the harder discipline of consistently rewarding the initiative itself rather than only the outcome. It closes by framing a genuinely proactive team as one of the most rewarding assets a leader can build, since such teams "prepare more than they repair."
points: Proactivity is shaped by leader behavior, not personality, team members take initiative when it's explicitly expected and recognized.
Leaders must reward the act of initiative itself, even when the outcome is disappointing, or team members will stop taking the risk.
Group brainstorming about upcoming events and possible pre-emptive actions is recommended as a concrete way to practice proactive thinking together.
Many work environments unintentionally punish initiative, which is why leaders must explicitly state that taking the initiative is expected and valued.
quotes: Every leader wants a team of proactive colleagues who anticipate needs, issues, and opportunities and step up to address them without being asked.
People anticipate and take the initiative when two things exist: an expectation that they should do so, and recognition for being proactive even when the outcome of their effort is less than desired.
Because many leaders and team environments punish initiative, leaders must highlight how important it is.

Good leaders reward the initiative, not the outcome. Sure, it’s essential to highlight how much easier, better, or more effective a given project turned out because of a team member’s proactive choices.
They prepare more than they repair, and that is a boon to leaders.
